articles.title: Cassini's Ice Grains From Enceladus Were Stranger Than Expected — And Now We Know Why
articles.summary: Ice grains erupting from Saturn's moon Enceladus had wildly different salt recipes, even though they came from one ocean. Lab experiments reveal freezing speed is the secret.

articles.title: Tagged Galápagos Turtles Surprised Scientists by Staying Put for Years
articles.summary: Nine green sea turtles in the Galápagos were tagged for up to 418 days. None left the marine reserve. Scientists expected long migrations — instead, the turtles stayed close to home.

articles.title: Tiny Diamond Anvils Reveal Iron Minerals That Could Store Earth's Primordial Water
articles.summary: Scientists discovered two new iron minerals that can hold water at extreme pressures near Earth's core. They might explain how our planet's oceans formed — and how water moves deep underground.
